slides.title: Where Observational Studies Come From
bullets: Company-sponsored: designed internally, run by clinical study or HEOR teams
Academic or scientific-society studies, governed more like an IIS
Both are observational rather than interventional in nature
MSLs support both, always within non-promotional limits

slides.title: Existing Records or a Real-Practice Cohort
bullets: Often draw on EHRs, insurer or hospital databases, disease registries
Or prospectively track a cohort already on standard treatment
The study never modifies the patient's actual care
That non-intervention is what separates it from a clinical trial legally

slides.title: Value at Every Stage
bullets: Design: share field clinical questions with internal evidence teams
Recruitment: inform investigators of studies open to their site
Always through formal channels, never as a commercial approach
Dissemination: help findings reach the right audience with context

slides.title: Robust Evidence Takes Years
bullets: Unlike a trial's fixed timeline, cohorts need years to mature
Sufficient size and exposure time are needed for robust results
Managing HCP expectations about that timeline is part of the MSL role

slides.title: The Bridge to Real Patients
bullets: Observational studies answer how a treatment works in real patients
They bridge controlled trial evidence and everyday clinical reality
Understanding methodology lets an MSL explain what a study can answer
And just as honestly, what it cannot answer yet

takeaway.title: Observational studies bridge trial evidence and real practice, and the MSL supports them at every stage without crossing into promotion
bullets: Non-intervention is what defines and protects this study type legally
MSL value spans design input, recruitment, and honest dissemination
Robust results take years, and setting that expectation is part of the job
